name: Luxor Nile river-form study
summary: A schematic wandering/braided Nile corridor with sediment bars, several flow paths and floodplain margins. It illustrates the older local river regime, not a recovered 2200 BCE plan of Thebes.
scaleNote: Landscape dimensions are illustrative. No measured settlement boundary, population or georeferenced ancient watercourse is asserted.

features.label: Vegetation & cultivation
features.text: River-supported fields, marshes, levees and wooded margins contrast with desert. Adaïma charcoal supports a local early wooded-margin interpretation, not an Egypt-wide closed forest. Report pages 2, 3.

features.label: Water & landform
features.text: The Delta, Giza, Luxor and Middle Egypt have different records. At Luxor a wandering/braided river preceded less-dynamic straight/anabranching channels; the modern single-thread local planform postdates the atlas interval. Report pages 2, 3.

features.label: What is not reconstructed
features.text: Do not transfer the Luxor core history directly to Amarna. Exact branch positions and Egypt-wide forest percentages are not supplied. Sediment dates are approximate. No species inventory is supplied for this scene; no animated wildlife or livestock has been added. Report pages 2, 3.
